sentences.text: The only known specimen of Protarchaeopteryx is the partial skeleton NGMC 2125, which represents a turkey-sized animal measuring one meter in length and seventy centimeters in height.
This creature possessed well-developed, vaned feathers extending from a relatively short tail, along with symmetrical feathers on its long, light forelimbs.
Its hands were long and slender, featuring three fingers with sharp, curved claws, while the animal also possessed a nascent beak, legs adapted for speed, and an elongated head.
Protarchaeopteryx possessed hollow, bird-like bones and a wishbone, structural features common in modern birds.

The name Protarchaeopteryx means "before Archaeopteryx," despite the fact that it lived in the Cretaceous while Archaeopteryx lived in the Jurassic, and it would have been larger than Archaeopteryx at around one meter in length.
In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated a lower body mass of 1.6 kilograms and a length of 0.7 meters for Protarchaeopteryx.
The genus Protarchaeopteryx was described by Q. Ji and S. Ji in 1997, with the only known species within the genus being Protarchaeopteryx robusta.
Protarchaeopteryx was likely a herbivore or omnivore.

It is assumed that Protarchaeopteryx was flightless because its skeletal structure would not support flapping flight, and because modern birds with symmetrical feathers cannot fly, it is considered a terrestrial animal.
Researchers have suggested that Protarchaeopteryx may have had an arboreal lifestyle, using its forelimbs for parachuting from tree limbs.

Protarchaeopteryx is classified within the infraorder Oviraptorosauria, the parent group for the genus, and is classified as a non-avian theropod and not a true bird, falling within the class Reptilia.
Protarchaeopteryx is closely related to the genus Incisivosaurus.

Protarchaeopteryx lived approximately 124.6 million years ago during the early Aptian age of the Early Cretaceous, and also lived approximately 124 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Middle Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
Fossils of Protarchaeopteryx have been found in the Jianshangou bed of the Yixian Formation in China.
The time range for Protarchaeopteryx is estimated from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago, spanning the Barremian to Aptian stages.
